headline: Greece has drafted a law that would require new data centers to get at least 60% of their electricity from renewable sources.
score_reason: Clear draft with detail, but still a proposal open to public comment.
importance_line: Data center investors in Greece would pay their own grid costs and post guarantees, but the rules are only a draft until public comment closes on 24 Oct.
summary: TaiyangNews reports that Greece's Ministry of Environment and Energy has drafted a law requiring new data centers to cover at least 60% of their annual electricity use with renewables, and to pay for grid connections and post a bank guarantee of 200,000 euros per megawatt. The draft is open to public comment until 24 Oct 2026 and is not yet law.
